<reason>CON won by judging the motion as written: PRO’s no-collapse evidence was narrow voluntary tracking prevention, not mandated system-level ad-and-tracker blocking, and PRO never pinned down who defines “robust” under liability. PRO had the cleaner consent/defaults story and a strong two-claims attack, but CON answered it and offered a tighter alternative (antitrust for Chrome, not a floor on every OS). A clipped CON opening keeps this competitive, not a rout.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2 (A4.3–A4.5): Safari/Firefox shipped limited tracking prevention, not ad blocking, so their survival does not prove the maximal mandate is safe or necessary.</best_rebuttal>
